10/10, my therapist quit.
Russian 12-year-olds call me 'cyka' while a spinbotter with 3 minutes played headshots me through the map and my will to live. Teammates: one god, four potatoes with aim like my ex. Went 2-27 and cried in spawn like a newborn.
Hate it more than my life choices, yet played 12 more hours after rage-uninstalling.
This isn’t a game, it’s Stockholm syndrome with worse hitreg.
Uninstalling tomorrow… right after one more match where I get owned.

positive.original:
After many hours playing CS2, I came to a simple conclusion:

You open the game thinking, “Just one quick match.”  
Five hours later you're arguing strategy with people you've never met, a Russian guy is yelling in the microphone, someone is blaming the tickrate, and somehow you're still clicking “Play Again.”

CS2 basically took everything that made Counter-Strike addictive and made it look better… while keeping the same level of stress.

Every match feels like the perfect mix of strategy, chaos, and that one teammate who buys an AWP every round but can't hit a single shot.

Pros:  
* Extremely precise gameplay  
* Intense rounds that get your heart racing  
* When the team actually works together, the game feels amazing

Cons:  
* There is always one guy rushing alone  
* Your rank will make you question your life choices  
* “Just one more match” is never just one

Final verdict:  
Highly recommended.  
Just be ready to love it, hate it, and keep playing anyway.

positive.original:
I have spent an unhealthy, borderline medically fascinating amount of time in Counter-Strike 2. Not “oh I played it for a weekend” time. I mean “I now measure real life distances in bombsite rotations” time. So believe me when I say this review comes from a place of deep experience and mild emotional damage.

🎯 [b]Gameplay: “Did I miss, or did reality glitch?”[/b]

Counter-Strike 2 feels like the developers took the precise, razor-sharp gunplay of CS:GO and ran it through a washing machine labeled “experimental physics + vibes.”

I’ll line up a perfect headshot. Crosshair planted. Breathing stopped. Inner peace achieved.

I click.

Nothing.

Then I die.

The killcam shows me aiming at a different postal code.

At this point, I’m not playing a shooter—I’m participating in a philosophical debate about what “hitting something” even means.

💨 [b]Sub-tick System: Schrödinger’s Bullet[/b]

Ah yes, the famous sub-tick system. Bullets now exist in a quantum state where they both hit and don’t hit until the server decides your emotional stability has suffered enough.

Sometimes it feels amazing. Crisp. Instant. Like the game read your mind.

Other times, I swear my bullets are politely asking enemies for consent before dealing damage.

🧠 [b]Matchmaking: A Social Experiment Gone Wrong[/b]

Matchmaking is less of a competitive system and more of a randomized psychological endurance test.

Your team will include:

- One guy who thinks he’s playing a stealth game and hasn’t bought a weapon since 2007
- One player with god-tier aim but the communication skills of a brick
- One person whose microphone sounds like it’s inside a washing machine full of gravel
- One toxic russian
- And you… questioning your life choices

Meanwhile, the enemy team is a coordinated five-stack who communicate using military callouts, telepathy, and what I assume is a shared brain.

🎤 [b]Voice Chat: ASMR From the Void[/b]

Voice chat deserves its own category of horror.

I have heard:

- Someone eating what sounded like raw concrete
- A full family argument in the background
- A smoke alarm with a personal vendetta
- A guy breathing like he just sprinted a marathon… while standing still in spawn

At one point, I genuinely forgot I was playing a game and thought I had accidentally joined a live documentary titled “Humans at Their Worst.”

💣 [b]Smokes: Now With Advanced Fluid Dynamics™[/b]

The new smoke system is cool. Very cool.

Too cool.

Smokes now behave like sentient beings. You throw one, and it reacts like:
“Interesting choice. I will now expand in ways you did not intend.”

You shoot through it? It opens.
You look at it funny? It shifts.
You trust it? Big mistake.

At this point, smokes are less “tactical tools” and more “unpredictable weather systems.”

🖥️ [b]Performance: A Rollercoaster of Regret[/b]

Sometimes the game runs beautifully.

Other times, my FPS drops harder than my confidence after missing a full magazine at point-blank range.

I’ve optimized settings, sacrificed background apps, whispered kind words to my GPU… and still, occasionally, the game decides:
“Today you play in PowerPoint mode.”

🎨 [b]Visuals: Shiny but Suspicious[/b]

Yes, the game looks better. Lighting is great. Models are clean.

But somehow, I can’t see enemies.

They blend into walls like they’re part of the décor. I’ve died to people who I’m convinced were legally classified as furniture.

🧍 [b]Movement: Ice Skating Simulator[/b]

Movement feels like I’m wearing socks on a freshly waxed floor.

I try to counter-strafe and instead perform a graceful slide into my own demise.

Enemies, meanwhile, peek corners with the precision of Olympic athletes.

I peek, and it looks like I tripped over my own expectations.

🧩 [b]Bugs: Features in Disguise[/b]

I have witnessed things in this game that cannot be explained by science:

- Grenades that vanish into alternate dimensions
- Players teleporting like they unlocked fast travel
- Sound cues that suggest the enemy is behind me, above me, and emotionally inside me

At this point, I don’t report bugs—I document paranormal activity.

❤️ [b]Why I Still Play[/b]

Despite everything… I keep coming back.

Because buried under the chaos, the confusion, and the occasional existential crisis… there is still that one perfect round.

The one where everything clicks.

You hit your shots.
Your team communicates.
The plan works.

And for a brief, beautiful moment, you feel like a tactical genius instead of a confused potato with a rifle.

⭐ [b]Final Verdict[/b]

Counter-Strike 2 is like a toxic relationship:

- It hurts you
- It confuses you
- It makes you question reality

But every now and then, it does something incredible… and you think:
“Maybe it’s changed.”

It hasn’t.

🧾 [b]Rating:[/b]

“I uninstalled it three times this week” / 10

Would I recommend it?

Yes.

But only if you enjoy:

- Emotional instability
- Questionable physics
- And yelling “HOW DID THAT NOT HIT??” at 2 AM

Now if you’ll excuse me, I have another match to queue.

I hate this game.

positive.english:
I have spent an unhealthy, borderline medically fascinating amount of time in Counter-Strike 2. Not “oh I played it for a weekend” time. I mean “I now measure real life distances in bombsite rotations” time. So believe me when I say this review comes from a place of deep experience and mild emotional damage.

🎯 [b]Gameplay: “Did I miss, or did reality glitch?”[/b]

Counter-Strike 2 feels like the developers took the precise, razor-sharp gunplay of CS:GO and ran it through a washing machine labeled “experimental physics + vibes.”

I’ll line up a perfect headshot. Crosshair planted. Breathing stopped. Inner peace achieved.

I click.

Nothing.

Then I die.

The killcam shows me aiming at a different postal code.

At this point, I’m not playing a shooter—I’m participating in a philosophical debate about what “hitting something” even means.

💨 [b]Sub-tick System: Schrödinger’s Bullet[/b]

Ah yes, the famous sub-tick system. Bullets now exist in a quantum state where they both hit and don’t hit until the server decides your emotional stability has suffered enough.

Sometimes it feels amazing. Crisp. Instant. Like the game read your mind.

Other times, I swear my bullets are politely asking enemies for consent before dealing damage.

🧠 [b]Matchmaking: A Social Experiment Gone Wrong[/b]

Matchmaking is less of a competitive system and more of a randomized psychological endurance test.

Your team will include:

- One guy who thinks he’s playing a stealth game and hasn’t bought a weapon since 2007
- One player with god-tier aim but the communication skills of a brick
- One person whose microphone sounds like it’s inside a washing machine full of gravel
- One toxic russian
- And you… questioning your life choices

Meanwhile, the enemy team is a coordinated five-stack who communicate using military callouts, telepathy, and what I assume is a shared brain.

🎤 [b]Voice Chat: ASMR From the Void[/b]

Voice chat deserves its own category of horror.

I have heard:

- Someone eating what sounded like raw concrete
- A full family argument in the background
- A smoke alarm with a personal vendetta
- A guy breathing like he just sprinted a marathon… while standing still in spawn

At one point, I genuinely forgot I was playing a game and thought I had accidentally joined a live documentary titled “Humans at Their Worst.”

💣 [b]Smokes: Now With Advanced Fluid Dynamics™[/b]

The new smoke system is cool. Very cool.

Too cool.

Smokes now behave like sentient beings. You throw one, and it reacts like:
“Interesting choice. I will now expand in ways you did not intend.”

You shoot through it? It opens.
You look at it funny? It shifts.
You trust it? Big mistake.

At this point, smokes are less “tactical tools” and more “unpredictable weather systems.”

🖥️ [b]Performance: A Rollercoaster of Regret[/b]

Sometimes the game runs beautifully.

Other times, my FPS drops harder than my confidence after missing a full magazine at point-blank range.

I’ve optimized settings, sacrificed background apps, whispered kind words to my GPU… and still, occasionally, the game decides:
“Today you play in PowerPoint mode.”

🎨 [b]Visuals: Shiny but Suspicious[/b]

Yes, the game looks better. Lighting is great. Models are clean.

But somehow, I can’t see enemies.

They blend into walls like they’re part of the décor. I’ve died to people who I’m convinced were legally classified as furniture.

🧍 [b]Movement: Ice Skating Simulator[/b]

Movement feels like I’m wearing socks on a freshly waxed floor.

I try to counter-strafe and instead perform a graceful slide into my own demise.

Enemies, meanwhile, peek corners with the precision of Olympic athletes.

I peek, and it looks like I tripped over my own expectations.

🧩 [b]Bugs: Features in Disguise[/b]

I have witnessed things in this game that cannot be explained by science:

- Grenades that vanish into alternate dimensions
- Players teleporting like they unlocked fast travel
- Sound cues that suggest the enemy is behind me, above me, and emotionally inside me

At this point, I don’t report bugs—I document paranormal activity.

❤️ [b]Why I Still Play[/b]

Despite everything… I keep coming back.

Because buried under the chaos, the confusion, and the occasional existential crisis… there is still that one perfect round.

The one where everything clicks.

You hit your shots.
Your team communicates.
The plan works.

And for a brief, beautiful moment, you feel like a tactical genius instead of a confused potato with a rifle.

⭐ [b]Final Verdict[/b]

Counter-Strike 2 is like a toxic relationship:

- It hurts you
- It confuses you
- It makes you question reality

But every now and then, it does something incredible… and you think:
“Maybe it’s changed.”

It hasn’t.

🧾 [b]Rating:[/b]

“I uninstalled it three times this week” / 10

Would I recommend it?

Yes.

But only if you enjoy:

- Emotional instability
- Questionable physics
- And yelling “HOW DID THAT NOT HIT??” at 2 AM

Now if you’ll excuse me, I have another match to queue.

I hate this game.

See you tomorrow.

I have spent an unhealthy, borderline medically fascinating amount of time in Counter-Strike 2. Not “oh I played it for a weekend” time. I mean “I now measure real life distances in bombsite rotations” time. So believe me when I say this review comes from a place of deep experience and mild emotional damage.

🎯 [b]Gameplay: “Did I miss, or did reality glitch?”[/b]

Counter-Strike 2 feels like the developers took the precise, razor-sharp gunplay of CS:GO and ran it through a washing machine labeled “experimental physics + vibes.”

I’ll line up a perfect headshot. Crosshair planted. Breathing stopped. Inner peace achieved.

I click.

Nothing.

Then I die.

The killcam shows me aiming at a different postal code.

At this point, I’m not playing a shooter—I’m participating in a philosophical debate about what “hitting something” even means.

💨 [b]Sub-tick System: Schrödinger’s Bullet[/b]

Ah yes, the famous sub-tick system. Bullets now exist in a quantum state where they both hit and don’t hit until the server decides your emotional stability has suffered enough.

Sometimes it feels amazing. Crisp. Instant. Like the game read your mind.

Other times, I swear my bullets are politely asking enemies for consent before dealing damage.

🧠 [b]Matchmaking: A Social Experiment Gone Wrong[/b]

Matchmaking is less of a competitive system and more of a randomized psychological endurance test.

Your team will include:

- One guy who thinks he’s playing a stealth game and hasn’t bought a weapon since 2007
- One player with god-tier aim but the communication skills of a brick
- One person whose microphone sounds like it’s inside a washing machine full of gravel
- One toxic russian
- And you… questioning your life choices

Meanwhile, the enemy team is a coordinated five-stack who communicate using military callouts, telepathy, and what I assume is a shared brain.

🎤 [b]Voice Chat: ASMR From the Void[/b]

Voice chat deserves its own category of horror.

I have heard:

- Someone eating what sounded like raw concrete
- A full family argument in the background
- A smoke alarm with a personal vendetta
- A guy breathing like he just sprinted a marathon… while standing still in spawn

At one point, I genuinely forgot I was playing a game and thought I had accidentally joined a live documentary titled “Humans at Their Worst.”

💣 [b]Smokes: Now With Advanced Fluid Dynamics™[/b]

The new smoke system is cool. Very cool.

Too cool.

Smokes now behave like sentient beings. You throw one, and it reacts like:
“Interesting choice. I will now expand in ways you did not intend.”

You shoot through it? It opens.
You look at it funny? It shifts.
You trust it? Big mistake.

At this point, smokes are less “tactical tools” and more “unpredictable weather systems.”

🖥️ [b]Performance: A Rollercoaster of Regret[/b]

Sometimes the game runs beautifully.

Other times, my FPS drops harder than my confidence after missing a full magazine at point-blank range.

I’ve optimized settings, sacrificed background apps, whispered kind words to my GPU… and still, occasionally, the game decides:
“Today you play in PowerPoint mode.”

🎨 [b]Visuals: Shiny but Suspicious[/b]

Yes, the game looks better. Lighting is great. Models are clean.

But somehow, I can’t see enemies.

They blend into walls like they’re part of the décor. I’ve died to people who I’m convinced were legally classified as furniture.

🧍 [b]Movement: Ice Skating Simulator[/b]

Movement feels like I’m wearing socks on a freshly waxed floor.

I try to counter-strafe and instead perform a graceful slide into my own demise.

Enemies, meanwhile, peek corners with the precision of Olympic athletes.

I peek, and it looks like I tripped over my own expectations.

🧩 [b]Bugs: Features in Disguise[/b]

I have witnessed things in this game that cannot be explained by science:

- Grenades that vanish into alternate dimensions
- Players teleporting like they unlocked fast travel
- Sound cues that suggest the enemy is behind me, above me, and emotionally inside me

At this point, I don’t report bugs—I document paranormal activity.

❤️ [b]Why I Still Play[/b]

Despite everything… I keep coming back.

Because buried under the chaos, the confusion, and the occasional existential crisis… there is still that one perfect round.

The one where everything clicks.

You hit your shots.
Your team communicates.
The plan works.

And for a brief, beautiful moment, you feel like a tactical genius instead of a confused potato with a rifle.

⭐ [b]Final Verdict[/b]

Counter-Strike 2 is like a toxic relationship:

- It hurts you
- It confuses you
- It makes you question reality

But every now and then, it does something incredible… and you think:
“Maybe it’s changed.”

It hasn’t.

🧾 [b]Rating:[/b]

“I uninstalled it three times this week” / 10

Would I recommend it?

Yes.

But only if you enjoy:

- Emotional instability
- Questionable physics
- And yelling “HOW DID THAT NOT HIT??” at 2 AM

Now if you’ll excuse me, I have another match to queue.

I hate this game.

See you tomorrow.

positive.original:
[b]Jumping into Counter-Strike 2 in 2026 is like revisiting a famously strict boarding school that recently got a beautiful visual overhaul but kept all of its most terrifying disciplinarians. Built on the gorgeous Source 2 engine, the game is visually stunning, featuring dynamic, volumetric smoke grenades that practically deserve their own casting credits and pristine lighting that perfectly illuminates every poor tactical decision you make. Yet, beneath the shiny new coat of paint, it remains the exact same ruthless, hyper-competitive trial by fire that has been systematically humbling gamers for well over two decades. There is absolutely no hand-holding here, your survival depends entirely on map knowledge, crisp crosshair placement, and the psychological fortitude to handle teammates who expect you to play like a seasoned esports professional in a casual Tuesday night lobby.

The core gameplay loop remains an addictive masterpiece of tension and release, but Valve continuously tweaks the formula to ensure nobody gets too comfortable. Recent updates have thrown a massive wrench into the muscle memory of veterans by introducing a realistic magazine reloading mechanic, meaning that if you habitually reload after firing a single warning shot, you will now unceremoniously throw the rest of your precious bullets directly into the trash. It is a hilarious and brutal way to force better ammo management, leading to countless moments of sheer panic as players realize their guns are completely empty during a crucial push. Combine that with the highly debated sub-tick server architecture and newly refined movement mechanics, and you have a tactical shooter that demands absolute precision while actively laughing at your attempts to master it.

As a free-to-play juggernaut, the game undeniably carries the classic baggage of massive online titles, from a wildly volatile matchmaking experience to an ongoing, exhausting arms race against cheaters. The learning curve is practically a vertical cliff, and you will spend your first few dozen hours spectating other players while trying to figure out why standing slightly to the left got you instantly eliminated through a wall. However, if you can push through the initial frustration, learn to ignore the occasionally toxic team communications, and embrace the sheer dopamine rush of landing a perfect one-tap headshot, you will quickly understand why millions of people absolutely refuse to play anything else. It is a brilliant, agonizing, beautifully updated playground that will consistently make you swear you are uninstalling forever, right before you immediately queue up for just one more match.[/b]

positive.original:
Counter Strike is basically a super competitive and very challenging FPS game,as the most popular FPS game in the world,it could be called the best among the FPS game history. I’m such a player who has been playing CS since CS:GO,it’s been 3 years since I played it. 1800hrs game time already showed how much I love this game. From simple skill groups to premier rating. From silver1 to 17k rating. It shows a normal and regular player’s growth process. Can’t believe it’s been 3 years already from a rookie who couldn’t even walk correctly to a player who can pull off 1v5 clutch sometimes. 
At the same time,it’s very usual to see different types of players here:toxic,friendly,kind,dramatic,hilarious,also someone who’s carrying without saying any word. They make my day(sometimes the opposite lol) 
To make a summary of my review ,let me say something for real: it’s a hard time when you’re in the battlefield,you’d better be ready for everything coming to you. Be yourself and ignore outside noises,you’ll become the better one you want to be:AWPer,fragger,supporter,lurker or IGL.
Always be ready for your day soldier.
Precision over power. Patience over haste.

positive.original:
CS2 is a great game, one of the best competitive tactical FPS games of all time — if not the best.

The game is in a pretty good state right now. There are fewer cheaters than there were around release, and the servers are working well.

The biggest issue at the moment is matchmaking. Sometimes you end up against strange 5-stacks with huge ELO gaps (like one 5k player, a couple around 15k, and two 25k+), and you’re playing for something like +100 / -500, which feels really frustrating.

Also, like in any competitive game, other players can ruin the experience — whether it’s toxicity, cheating, or griefing. That’s just something you have to accept.

If you play CS2 casually, you’ll probably love it. If you play it regularly, you’ll both love it and hate it.

positive.original:
I load in thinking I’m locked in, then immediately lose the first gunfight and spend the rest of the match trying to mentally recover. Some rounds I look decent, other rounds I’m getting one-tapped so fast I’m not even sure I left spawn.

I swear the game can tell when I’m feeling confident too. The second I think “okay I’m playing well,” I whiff something so bad I just sit there for a second like… yeah that checks out.

Teammates are always a gamble. Either you get chill people and the game is actually fun, or you get a full-time critic watching your every move like it’s a live performance.

Best part is I’ll be annoyed the entire match, say I’m done after, then instantly queue again like I learned nothing.

Good game, terrible for my ego. 10/10

positive.original:
It is one of the best strategy games I have ever played. What makes it especially interesting is how much it focuses on utility and timing rather than just aim. Using smokes, flashes, and molotovs at the right moment can completely change the outcome of a round. It reminds me of the older days of gaming, when developers prioritized gameplay and balance over monetization.

I would definitely recommend it to anyone who enjoys tactical, skill-based games. It’s especially worth playing if you like teamwork, strategy, and a fair competitive experience.

positive.original: Counter-Strike 2 is a modern evolution of the classic tactical shooter formula, bringing improved visuals, more realistic lighting, and updated mechanics while staying true to its competitive roots. The new sub-tick system makes actions feel more responsive, and the redesigned smoke grenades add fresh strategic depth by interacting dynamically with the environment. While the core gameplay remains as intense and skill-based as ever, the game still faces some issues, including performance inconsistencies, bugs, and mixed feedback on movement and hit registration compared to CS:GO. Overall, CS2 is a solid upgrade that successfully refreshes the experience without losing what made Counter-Strike iconic, though it still has room to improve.

positive.original:
Counter-Strike 2 is a really good game, no doubt. The gameplay is fun and competitive, but man… it can get stressful sometimes 😅 One round you’re feeling like a pro, next round you’re questioning your whole life.

Honestly, it’s way better when you play with friends. You can joke around, communicate, and even when things go bad, it’s still fun instead of pure stress. Solo queue = stress mode, friends = fun mode.

Overall, great game, just grab your squad and enjoy it 👍

Only real issue is the cheaters sometimes — that can be frustrating — but aside from that, it’s still one of the best competitive games out there.

negative.original: Why the hell would an FPS game destroy the pure, unadulterated fun of shooting? The competition and mind game in a shooter should be about positioning, tactics, and actual skill—not about restricting how you fire your gun, controlling every single shot you take, and limiting how you move. Why does Valve always feel the need to dictate how I play the game? Why do you keep forcing your rules on me, telling me how to shoot, how to move, how to have fun? You’re not balancing the game—you’re killing the core joy of what makes an FPS an FPS. We don’t need you to train us or discipline us on how to play. We just want to shoot, compete, and enjoy the game we love. Stop ruining Counter-Strike with these pointless, restrictive changes that only suck all the fun out of the gunfight.

negative.original: The more I play the more I realize just how incompetent and deaf this company is. If you want a cheater free experience you need to involve a third party website that will have its own better anticheat and a much better PERFORMANCE based ELO system. Still have no implemented original maps from CSGO, cut all community servers, movement and shooting is horrible and performance tanks for no reason. Out of all the glaring issues that plague this game we are rolling out a patch for... ammo economy? They also just could not stand people trading on third party websites (so they could avoid a TWENTY percent sale tax this filth of a company has)  so they added terminals where you will have to spend up to steam wallet max(like 1.6k) to purchase a skin in case you actually roll gold. They have no interest in player satisfaction or the state of the game. They are allergic to doing anything that requires a modicum amount of effort and are blind to most glaring issues for over 2 years.

negative.original: The developers of this game do not care about the user base. They constantly push cosmetics to make as much $ as possible all while ignoring their communities biggest wishes to make the game better. No working anticheat, no better tick servers. Fewer community servers/workshop maps than CSGO. And ontop of all of this, they continue to push bs updates that nobody asks for instead of focusing on the changes the players actually want. The recent bs reload update was the nail in the coffin for me. Death to cs2, the game is already bleeding out.

negative.original:
Would not recommend to start this game anymore.

It once was one of the best games out there with lots of fun stuff to do and a thriving community full of modded servers and endless possibilities to enjoy the game in different ways like:

Surfing, Bhop, KZ Climb, Gungame, Zombie Escape, Prop Hunt, Minigames, Deathrun, Danger Zone ...
Basically everything died.
Surfing and Bhop doesnt really work anymore.
Gungame got replaced by this boring Arms race mod with only 2 maps while there where hundreds back in the day.

They had a great fundament for making maps and allowing the community to do whatever they wanted to just enjoy the game.

Then they started to monetize the ♥♥♥♥ out of the game and reduced everything back to this competitive ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ everyone is playing since years.
Lots of people that can´t get their life together and need to find meaning and fulfillment by climbing imaginary ranks just to feel some sense of accomplishment they cannot get in the real world.

Guess what guys, the grind never ends... There will always be someone better, there will always be a higher difficulty may it be on FACEIT or ESEA or whatever...
So why can so many people just not play a chill round of the game and enjoy the time with it.

Right now the game is just getting worse and worse with every meaningless update they put out.
You´re basically playing the same 10 maps you played 10 years ago that just got reworked 5 times each for no purpose at all, while there would be actually hundreds of maps that could get implemented just for the fun of playing.
Back in the day we used to play all these same maps in CS:Source and tons more like de_piranesi, de_cbble, de_prodigy and lots and lots more, which were definitely not suited for competitive gameplay and we still had a great time. 
So how does the same game series 10 - 15 years later have significantly less content than anything back then?

In some aspect we the players are of course part of the problem by supporting this downwards spiral with our money and toxic positivity for way too long!

And I won´t even address the whole cheater and bot situation, because thats just also so obviously bad since forever.

Let´s see where this all leads...
Can´t recommend this to anyone anymore.
Once a 10/10 game with a 10/10 community turned into a 0/10 game with a 1/10 community.
Rip CS:GO

Who the hell came up with the idea to replace bullets with magazines that CANNOT BE PRESERVED in COUNTER-STRIKE? 

CS always stood out because it was clearly a GAME with GAME MECHANICS - It never really went for realism in the tedious sense like this.

Give us back CS:GO if you want to make CS2 into a Temu immitation of Call of Duty... What will the next game breaking changes be? New "realistic" movement with stamina, go prone, lean and ADS? What about holding shift to steady your aim while you are at it?

Absolutely retarded, if you wanted to make a new tactical shooter, just do that - But why take away a classic of multiplayer competitive gaming like this? Revert this or the game will die completely. Also give me back dangerzone, that ♥♥♥♥ was funny AF.

negative.original:
Oh boy. Where do I even start.
This is one of the most unnecessary, game-feel-destroying changes Valve has pushed in years, and I say that as someone who's watched this franchise slowly drift away from what made it great.
This punishes good habits, not bad ones.
In classic CS, disciplined players always reloaded in a safe moment, behind cover, between rounds, after a peek. That was good play. Now you're being punished for being proactive. You fire three bullets holding an angle, you duck back, you top off, and now you just threw away 12 bullets? That's not adding depth, that's adding arbitrary tax on smart positioning.
The "trade-off" they invented doesn't exist in real CS.
CS is not a game about ammo scarcity. It never was. The economy is the scarcity mechanic. The money you spent on that AK and those bullets is the trade-off. Adding a secondary bullet economy on top of that doesn't create interesting decisions. It creates annoying micro-management that clutters reads and punishes newer players disproportionately.
This homogenizes CS with games it was never supposed to be.
Magazine-discard on reload is a mechanic from Battlefield, from Tarkov, from milsim games that want you to think about every round. CS was always about pure aim, positioning, and economy, not inventory simulation. This moves the needle toward a completely different genre identity.
It will destroy certain playstyles entirely.
AWPers who re-peek after a shot. Riflers holding close angles after a spray. Anyone who fires a burst and reloads to stay topped off, which is essentially every experienced player. The muscle memory that millions of players have built over 20+ years now works against them.
"Three clips" is not a meaningful answer.
That's 90 bullets on a rifle. Sounds fine until you're in a long B-site hold against a full buy round and you've burned through a mag and a half. The psychological pressure of watching those reserve mags disappear mid-round is not tension, it's distraction.
The stated reason is weak.
"The decision to reload should have higher stakes." Why? Who asked for this? Name one high-level player, one tournament, one community post that identified reloading as the low-stakes problem holding the game back. This is a solution to a problem that existed only on a Valve whiteboard.
The soul of CS has always been: simple rules, deep mastery. This adds complexity without depth. It's busywork dressed up as game design.

VALVE CAN YOU ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ CONCENTRATE ONCE AND BRING WHAT EVERYONE WANTS?
CACHE! ANTI CHEAT UPDATES! GAMEPLAY QoL CHANGES! NOT A ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ MILSIM FEATURE.

Wont play this game until this reverts. Pathetic.

This homogenizes CS with games it was never supposed to be.
Magazine-discard on reload is a mechanic from Battlefield, from Tarkov, from milsim games that want you to think about every round. CS was always about pure aim, positioning, and economy, not inventory simulation. This moves the needle toward a completely different genre identity.
It will destroy certain playstyles entirely.
AWPers who re-peek after a shot. Riflers holding close angles after a spray. Anyone who fires a burst and reloads to stay topped off, which is essentially every experienced player. The muscle memory that millions of players have built over 20+ years now works against them.
"Three clips" is not a meaningful answer.
That's 90 bullets on a rifle. Sounds fine until you're in a long B-site hold against a full buy round and you've burned through a mag and a half. The psychological pressure of watching those reserve mags disappear mid-round is not tension, it's distraction.
The stated reason is weak.
"The decision to reload should have higher stakes." Why? Who asked for this? Name one high-level player, one tournament, one community post that identified reloading as the low-stakes problem holding the game back. This is a solution to a problem that existed only on a Valve whiteboard.
The soul of CS has always been: simple rules, deep mastery. This adds complexity without depth. It's busywork dressed up as game design.

negative.original:
With every update, the game gets worse instead of better.
It increasingly feels broken, performance issues, questionable gameplay changes, and bugs that don’t get fixed but seem to multiply.

What’s especially frustrating is that things which previously worked fine become unstable or outright unplayable after updates. Any trust that updates will actually improve the game is completely gone at this point.

Instead of moving forward, the game feels like it’s taking steps backwards with every patch. It’s simply not fun anymore.

And to make things worse, while all of this is happening, the cheating problem still isn’t properly addressed. Instead of focusing on effective anti-cheat measures, the game keeps getting updated in ways that only make the overall experience worse.

negative.original:
In my opinion, in the past few months the game took a nosedive in terms of quality and support from the devs.
Still no 128 tick servers, slow server frame issues every other game, still no functional anticheat system, a large portion of the map pool was removed without any particular reason and I could go on for days to prove my point that valve will soon become like blizzard/ubisoft/EA... Once great companies getting brainwashed by greed and corporate decision making prioritizing profits over gamers.

Just take a look at the current state of affairs with terminals: They literally sell you THE POSSIBILITY to buy a skin from them... People are spending 10-15 euros on terminals just TO BE ABLE TO buy a skin from valve, yet every update the game gets worse gameplay wise, I mean what is the new ammo update? Nobody asked to change a core gameplay mechanic of a competitive game which has been going strong for more than 20 years

For now I'll stick with CS:GO, even if there are no official servers

negative.original:
I can’t recommend CS2 in its current state after the latest update.

The new reload system fundamentally changes how the game feels—and not in a good way. Losing all remaining bullets when reloading might sound like a “tactical” improvement on paper, but in practice it punishes years of built-in muscle memory that defined Counter-Strike’s core gameplay. Reloading has always been a natural, low-risk action between engagements. Now it’s something that can randomly cost you rounds, not because of poor decision-making, but because the game suddenly redefined a basic mechanic.

This isn’t just a small tweak—it disrupts the flow that made Counter-Strike so smooth and skill-based. Instead of rewarding precision and positioning, it introduces unnecessary friction and hesitation. Players are now second-guessing simple actions rather than focusing on aim, timing, and strategy.

Worse, it doesn’t feel like it adds meaningful depth. It just replaces a clean, intuitive system with something clunky and frustrating. There’s a difference between raising the skill ceiling and making the game less enjoyable to play—and this update leans heavily toward the latter.

Until this change is reconsidered or properly reworked, CS2 feels like a step backward rather than an evolution.

negative.original:
While CS2 introduced some neat technical details, like the improved weapon reload animations (which was great idea). The overall atmosphere feels like a massive downgrade. CS:GO felt like a gritty, mil-sim inspired tactical shooter. CS2, from its UI to its lighting, feels like a generic E-sports title. They say don't judge a book by its cover, but in this case, the cover reflects the content perfectly.

The Atmosphere Downgrade
The game is clearly optimized for the professional E-sports scene, you can hear it in soundtrack and see it in promo material and UI. The contrast is cranked up and everything is "over-brightened" to make it look good for spectators on a stream and for the colours to grab the attention of viewers. BUT the game DID NOT became world-wide favourite because it was generic colorfull overwatch/valorant-ahh shooter. It had its military direction, which makes me ask: Why change the style ? To appeal to the masses ? I think people, who dont like the "grim mil-sim" vibe that CSGO had to offer, shouldnt be playing these shooter games anyways. Its supposed to be game with realistic guns, graphics, topic. Its about counter-terrorism for crying out loud.

This shift explains why the broken anti-cheat isn't being fixed with any urgency. In the pro scene, matches are played on private, strictly monitored servers where cheating is nearly impossible. But for the average player? The game is borderline unplayable. I won't lie and say there’s a cheater in every single game, but looking back, it honestly feels like 4 out of 10 matches have cheaters who "dont even try to hide it".

And MOST IMPORTANTLY
The point isn't whether CS:GO had cheaters (it did btw). The point is that CS2 was marketed as a sequel. It was supposed to build on the foundations of its predecessor and improve them. The game had less features than CSGO on launch and now 2 and half years after release, new features barely made it up for the lost ones.
It’s hard to believe this game is made made by the same legendary Valve (that I still admire, might I add). Gabe Newell’s philosophy was always that a "game should not be ignoring the player". CS2 doesn't feel like it's made for the players anymore. It feels like it was made for the E-sports industry and the viewers. The fact that we are actually playing it seems like not even an afterthought but a side effect.

The point isn't whether CS:GO had cheaters (it did btw). The point is that CS2 was marketed as a sequel. It was supposed to build on the foundations of its predecessor and improve them. The game had less features than CSGO on launch and now 2 and half years after release, new features barely made it up for the lost ones.
It’s hard to believe this game is made made by the same legendary Valve (that I still admire, might I add). Gabe Newell’s philosophy was always that a "game should not be ignoring the player". CS2 doesn't feel like it's made for the players anymore. It feels like it was made for the E-sports industry and the viewers. The fact that we are actually playing it seems like not even an afterthought but a side effect.

negative.original:
I’ve been a passionate player of this game for years—specifically the original CS:GO. I’ve spent countless hours playing, improving, and enjoying the competitive aspect that made it so iconic.

The transition to CS2 was something I eventually got used to. At first, it felt different, but over time I accepted the changes and continued playing. However, the recent updates have pushed me to finally write this review.

The latest changes to Inferno are, in my opinion, terrible. The map no longer feels right, and while it hasn’t completely stopped me from playing, it definitely reduced the enjoyment.

But what really crossed the line is today’s update—the magazine system. This change completely broke the core mechanics of the game. Counter-Strike has had a consistent and well-established gameplay style for over a decade, and suddenly changing something this fundamental makes no sense.

I don’t understand what the developers are trying to achieve. Mechanics like magazine management belong in tactical shooters like Ready or Not, not in a competitive game where players expect precision, consistency, and familiarity.

This change feels illogical, unnecessary, and completely out of place. It doesn’t improve the game—it only makes it worse.

negative.original:
Biggest L update in CS history.
They took a core mechanic unchanged since 1999 and ruined it for no reason. Reloading now wastes EVERY leftover bullet in the mag—shoot 1 bullet then reload? Lose 29. Habit of topping off after a kill? Now you're throwing away ammo like an idiot. AWP reserve mags gutted to 2, turning the best gun into a pea shooter. M4A1-S feels even worse.
Community is screaming "revert" on Reddit, HLTV, everywhere—yet Valve ignores it. This kills the flow, the fun, the fast-paced gunplay that made CS legendary. It forces slow, boring, ammo-hoarding playstyle instead of aggressive peeks and trades.
Tried to adapt for hours—still feels wrong. Thousands of hours muscle memory deleted. Cheaters were bad enough, now the game itself punishes you for playing normally.
Thumbs down. Avoid until they fix this disaster.

This reload update will probably make at least the following legit gameplay styles in some pro matches significantly harder:
1. Smoke Spamming
2. Wallbanging
3. Prefiring
4. Using firing sounds as distractions
5. Using firing sounds to cover up footsteps
6. Using usp-s and m4a1-s
7. Playing clutches(especially trying to have a 1v5 ace)
8. Being sprayers rather than tappers(both were valid styles with their own pros and cons)
Imo, assuming that the community does hate reload cancers that much, changing the reloading mechanism still isn't the only way to add risk to reloading, as it can also be done by increasing reload times differently for each gun, which would lead to much easier balancing later on. That might still suck, but it'd still be much better than throwing an entire magazine away for most guns...
I rarely leave any negative review, and I'd be fine if the old way of reloading is kept but takes noticeably longer and the new way becomes a faster option, but with this ammo reload update, I think I'm just better off uninstalling CS2 and reinstalling CSGO instead :(

negative.original:
CS2 feels like it’s in one of the worst states I’ve seen any Counter-Strike game in years. The cheating problem is completely out of control. Match after match is filled with blatant hackers, and it honestly kills any motivation to queue up. What’s worse is that instead of addressing that core issue, we’re getting game play changes no one asked for.

The recent ammo changes feel totally tone deaf. They don’t improve the experience, they just add frustration and mess with a formula that didn’t need fixing. Meanwhile, the actual problems, anti-cheat, matchmaking integrity, are still being ignored.

Agents can also increase their skills, firearms can be modified, the magazine can be thrown out and smash people,and safe deposit boxes can be added to package points a and b to obtain better weapons. The magazine update has ruined the best FPS game. Let’s congratulate Valorant :) <3.

negative.original: Genuinely CS 2 is the biggest piece of horse dung I’ve ever played, I assumed maybe due nostalgia of CSGO that I happened to prefer CSGO. But after testing and experience I assure you that CSGO is still miles better than CS2. CS2, you have literal people running and AWPing mean while you attempt to spray point blank and the only thing you are able to hit is an out line of a ♥♥♥♥ around the person DESPITE YOU SEEING THE FACT YOU HIT HIM but it wouldn’t register due to presumably sub tick. I cannot express my deep inner rage that seems quite prevalent whenever I boot this game, because I know that I’m in it to suffer and terminate/pulverize my entire setup and potentially house to dust. Like genuinely is there only half a dev working on this game? What is going on? Where is Cache? Why are we only getting skin updates when the game is in this absurd purgatory state. The VAC anticheat just seemingly just doesn’t even work, on a lower trust factor account your legit guaranteed to run into at least one cheater and that’s being generous, and EVEN in higher trust factor your still going to encounter cheaters. I would rather go play with my own dookie and smear it across my entire house, and use it as a slip and slide then play this game. Actually, scratch that I would rather torture my own prostate while watching the cracks in the floor for more entertainment and peace then this game offers, like genuinely digging a dirt hole is more fun then playing this abomination of a game. I haven’t cried for years until I started playing this game again, I literally cried tears streaming down my face, I was crying out of my eyeballs out of pure sorrow and despair. We are in the big 2026 and we cannot even add Cache. The only thing this game has going for it is the free drops at the end of the week which you will make money on, but at this point id rather eat Shaquille O’Neal’s filthy disgusting rancid putrefying butt hole, after a musty disgusting fecal matter release than play this game to obtain said drops. Torture seems a lot better at this point or even total sensory deprivation as in removing your eyes, destroy your ear drums, remove your tongue, remove your hands, chop off your feet, and terminate your nervous system. Chickens are cute though.

Valve just made an update that ruined their own game by adding a useless magazine system and an incomplete, illogical reload system that is somehow even worse than Tarkov’s.

I suggest you all protest against Valve again over this update, because it is damaging their own community and pushing players away from a game they once loved, a game with a rich history and a reload system that had worked for decades.

If they really want to improve the game, why don’t they improve the anti-cheat and fix the subtick system instead of doing this?

This trash ammo update smells like it was pushed by a dev who unironically loves being a cuck and cries himself to sleep because nobody respects his "tacticool" extraction-shooter fantasies.

Imagine being so desperate for control that you force your trash update onto a player base that’s been fine without your input for 20 years. This isn't a balance patch; it’s a mid-life crisis from a beta who’s addicted to the "submission" of tedious mechanics.

negative.original:
I can confidently say I do not recommend Counter-Strike 2. The best part is the updates. Every time there’s one, you get a little bit of hope… maybe they fixed matchmaking? Maybe they dealt with cheaters? Maybe hit registration works like it exists in reality?
Nope.
They updated reloading.
Yes, reloading. Because clearly the biggest issue in the game was how the gun goes click clack instead of clack click. Meanwhile, everything actually wrong is sitting in the corner untouched like it’s part of the map design.
It’s honestly kind of amazing. Thousands of hours in, and the only consistent thing is disappointment. Every patch feels like they spun a wheel labeled “Important Fixes” and it only has one option: “Something Nobody Asked For.”

Yes, reloading. Because clearly the biggest issue in the game was how the gun goes click clack instead of clack click. Meanwhile, everything actually wrong is sitting in the corner untouched like it’s part of the map design.
It’s honestly kind of amazing. Thousands of hours in, and the only consistent thing is disappointment. Every patch feels like they spun a wheel labeled “Important Fixes” and it only has one option: “Something Nobody Asked For.”

negative.original:
This is arguably the worst iteration in Counter-Strike history. It feels like Valve has built a playground specifically for cheaters. Between the flawed sub-tick system and the lack of a proper anti-cheat, the game is currently in a disastrous state.

The "Legit" Cheating Problem
If your win rate climbs even slightly above 49%, prepare to face "pro" players in 90 out of 100 matches. These accounts follow a suspicious pattern:

15-year-old accounts with only 200–600 hours played.

Only 1–3 games in their library and a couple of friends.

Zero actual gaming activity or profile history.

These players have "built-in" wallhacks—they stack exactly where you are, kill you through smoke, and land blind headshots through three walls.

Failed Security (VAC)
Valve’s anti-cheat (VAC) is a joke. It seems to only detect bunnyhop scripts while completely ignoring blatant Aimbots and Triggerbots. You can report them, provide evidence, or post on the forums, but the community management is more likely to ban you for "spam" than to ban the actual cheaters.

Broken Matchmaking
The system doesn't reward skill; it punishes it. If you play better than the average player, you are immediately thrown into lobbies with "god-tier" cheaters who have been playing unpunished for years. Valve chooses to ignore the community's outcry because the game is Free-to-Play, and the skin market keeps the money flowing regardless of the game's integrity.

Bottom line: Don't waste your time or money. Until Valve implements a kernel-level anti-cheat or a functional Overwatch system, this game is nothing more than a cheating simulator.

negative.original:
Title: VAC is Useless, and This Game Is Wasting the People Who Actually Care

I have a love-hate relationship with CS2 right now.

Every update is a mixed bag—some good, some bad. I get it, no game is perfect. But what really drives me crazy is the so-called "anti-cheat" system, VAC. It might as well not exist.

It’s not even about suspecting someone is cheating anymore. You’ll have people openly admitting it in voice chat: "Yeah, I’m cheating. VAC won’t do anything. Worst case, I get a 24-hour cooldown, maybe seven days, and then I’m right back." You report them, and they keep playing match after match like nothing happened. VAC doesn’t even flinch.

What makes it worse is that I used to think I was just bad.

I’d lose a match, go back and watch the demo, analyzing every mistake—my counter-strafing was off, my crosshair placement was sloppy, my trades were slow. I spent hours every day practicing my aim, my movement, my pre-aiming, trying to improve every little detail so I could hold my own in matches.

Then I watch the replay. The enemy’s crosshair is tracking me through walls. I peek and get instantly one-tapped. No time to react.

I put in all that work to get better, and all it did was make cheaters stomp me more efficiently. Honestly, playing a game to the point where you start doubting yourself feels terrible. I can’t even tell anymore whether someone is genuinely skilled or just cheating.

Don’t get me wrong—CS2 is a great game at its core. The gunplay, the tactics, the map control… that’s all still there. But the current state of the competitive scene is a nightmare, especially for new players. Forget about telling newcomers to "just practice your aim" or "learn some utility." When every other match is full of blatant cheaters, you don’t even get a chance to play fair.

You could drop donk, ZywOo, or Niko into one of these lobbies, and they’d get destroyed too—not because they’re not skilled enough, but because the other team isn’t even pretending to play fair, and there’s nothing you can do about it.

When a competitive game reaches the point where players who actually put in the effort can’t even expect a fair match, it stops being competitive. It just burns you out.

I still play because I love this game. But if Valve keeps ignoring the state of VAC, soon the only people left will be cheaters and the players who haven’t given up yet.

Good game. Terrible environment. No one in charge seems to care.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

標題：VAC 形同虛設，這遊戲正在消耗真正想玩的人

我現在對《CS2》真的是又愛又恨。

每次更新，好壞參半，這我認了，畢竟沒有完美的遊戲。但真正讓我心寒的，是那個號稱「反作弊」的 VAC——它根本形同虛設。

已經不是「懷疑」對方有沒有開，而是對面直接開麥嗆聲：「我就是開了，VAC 抓不到啦，頂多冷卻24小時，再不然七天，出來我又是一條好漢。」檢舉了，看他繼續活蹦亂跳好幾場，VAC 連個反應都沒有。

更可悲的是，我一開始還以為是自己菜。

輸了之後反覆看 demo，檢討自己急停沒停好、預瞄點歪了、補槍慢了。我每天練急停、練定位、練預瞄，把細節一個一個摳出來，就為了能在對局裡站穩腳跟。

結果回放一看，對面準星隔著牆就跟著我走，跳出去瞬間爆頭，連反應時間都沒有。

總結：好遊戲，爛環境，沒人管。

Title: VAC is Useless, and This Game Is Wasting the People Who Actually Care

I have a love-hate relationship with CS2 right now.

Every update is a mixed bag—some good, some bad. I get it, no game is perfect. But what really drives me crazy is the so-called "anti-cheat" system, VAC. It might as well not exist.

It’s not even about suspecting someone is cheating anymore. You’ll have people openly admitting it in voice chat: "Yeah, I’m cheating. VAC won’t do anything. Worst case, I get a 24-hour cooldown, maybe seven days, and then I’m right back." You report them, and they keep playing match after match like nothing happened. VAC doesn’t even flinch.

What makes it worse is that I used to think I was just bad.

I’d lose a match, go back and watch the demo, analyzing every mistake—my counter-strafing was off, my crosshair placement was sloppy, my trades were slow. I spent hours every day practicing my aim, my movement, my pre-aiming, trying to improve every little detail so I could hold my own in matches.

Then I watch the replay. The enemy’s crosshair is tracking me through walls. I peek and get instantly one-tapped. No time to react.

I put in all that work to get better, and all it did was make cheaters stomp me more efficiently. Honestly, playing a game to the point where you start doubting yourself feels terrible. I can’t even tell anymore whether someone is genuinely skilled or just cheating.

Don’t get me wrong—CS2 is a great game at its core. The gunplay, the tactics, the map control… that’s all still there. But the current state of the competitive scene is a nightmare, especially for new players. Forget about telling newcomers to "just practice your aim" or "learn some utility." When every other match is full of blatant cheaters, you don’t even get a chance to play fair.

You could drop donk, ZywOo, or Niko into one of these lobbies, and they’d get destroyed too—not because they’re not skilled enough, but because the other team isn’t even pretending to play fair, and there’s nothing you can do about it.

When a competitive game reaches the point where players who actually put in the effort can’t even expect a fair match, it stops being competitive. It just burns you out.

I still play because I love this game. But if Valve keeps ignoring the state of VAC, soon the only people left will be cheaters and the players who haven’t given up yet.

Good game. Terrible environment. No one in charge seems to care.

每次更新，好壞參半，這我認了，畢竟沒有完美的遊戲。但真正讓我心寒的，是那個號稱「反作弊」的 VAC——它根本形同虛設。

已經不是「懷疑」對方有沒有開，而是對面直接開麥嗆聲：「我就是開了，VAC 抓不到啦，頂多冷卻24小時，再不然七天，出來我又是一條好漢。」檢舉了，看他繼續活蹦亂跳好幾場，VAC 連個反應都沒有。

更可悲的是，我一開始還以為是自己菜。

輸了之後反覆看 demo，檢討自己急停沒停好、預瞄點歪了、補槍慢了。我每天練急停、練定位、練預瞄，把細節一個一個摳出來，就為了能在對局裡站穩腳跟。

結果回放一看，對面準星隔著牆就跟著我走，跳出去瞬間爆頭，連反應時間都沒有。

我努力把自己練得更好，結果只是讓外掛把我按住在地上摩擦得更流暢。玩個遊戲玩到開始懷疑自己，這感覺真的很糟糕。我已經分不清對面是真的比我強，還是只是開了。

說真的，《CS2》的本質絕對是好玩的，槍法、戰術、地圖控制，這些核心樂趣還在。但現在這個遊戲環境，對新手來說根本是地獄。不要說什麼「新手要練槍、要學道具」，在滿是掛的場子裡，你連公平對槍的機會都沒有。

我看就算把 donk、ZywOo、Niko 這些頂尖明星選手請來，排在這種局裡，他們也照樣被打到懷疑人生——不是因為槍法不夠硬，是因為對面根本不演，而你毫無對抗手段。

當一個競技遊戲，讓認真投入的玩家連「公平」兩個字都不敢奢望的時候，這遊戲已經不是競技了，只是單純在消耗熱情。

我還在玩，是因為我愛這個遊戲。但如果 Valve 繼續放任 VAC 擺爛，那這款遊戲遲早只剩下開掛的人，和還在受苦的人。

總結：好遊戲，爛環境，沒人管。
translations.german:
Title: VAC is Useless, and This Game Is Wasting the People Who Actually Care

I have a love-hate relationship with CS2 right now.

Every update is a mixed bag—some good, some bad. I get it, no game is perfect. But what really drives me crazy is the so-called "anti-cheat" system, VAC. It might as well not exist.

It’s not even about suspecting someone is cheating anymore. You’ll have people openly admitting it in voice chat: "Yeah, I’m cheating. VAC won’t do anything. Worst case, I get a 24-hour cooldown, maybe seven days, and then I’m right back." You report them, and they keep playing match after match like nothing happened. VAC doesn’t even flinch.

What makes it worse is that I used to think I was just bad.

I’d lose a match, go back and watch the demo, analyzing every mistake—my counter-strafing was off, my crosshair placement was sloppy, my trades were slow. I spent hours every day practicing my aim, my movement, my pre-aiming, trying to improve every little detail so I could hold my own in matches.

Then I watch the replay. The enemy’s crosshair is tracking me through walls. I peek and get instantly one-tapped. No time to react.

I put in all that work to get better, and all it did was make cheaters stomp me more efficiently. Honestly, playing a game to the point where you start doubting yourself feels terrible. I can’t even tell anymore whether someone is genuinely skilled or just cheating.

Don’t get me wrong—CS2 is a great game at its core. The gunplay, the tactics, the map control… that’s all still there. But the current state of the competitive scene is a nightmare, especially for new players. Forget about telling newcomers to "just practice your aim" or "learn some utility." When every other match is full of blatant cheaters, you don’t even get a chance to play fair.

You could drop donk, ZywOo, or Niko into one of these lobbies, and they’d get destroyed too—not because they’re not skilled enough, but because the other team isn’t even pretending to play fair, and there’s nothing you can do about it.

When a competitive game reaches the point where players who actually put in the effort can’t even expect a fair match, it stops being competitive. It just burns you out.

I still play because I love this game. But if Valve keeps ignoring the state of VAC, soon the only people left will be cheaters and the players who haven’t given up yet.

Good game. Terrible environment. No one in charge seems to care.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

negative.original:
As a person with adhd, i have always struggeled a bit when playing cs2. But with the new Reload Update, the game is borderline unplayable for me. 

This is not an ocd issue, i don't reload just because i want to see a full mag. It's me knowing that i will need 5 more Bullets in the gunfight that is sure to come, 30 seconds in the future.

This game has never been Realistic. I neither expect nor want it to be. If i wanted something harder with more intricate mechanics i would switch games. 

Also i cannot understand how RELOADING is the most important thing on the agenda. 
- I have been experiencing crashes every third game, have'nt seen a single Game without someone getting kicked from the game.
- There is an ongoing cheater problem, there is a good reason many people prefer faceit.
- The Community has been BEGGING for new Maps for Months
- Server Downtime has become way to regular
and im absolutely sure other players have even more to say.

Fundamentaly changing Gameplay was not what i expected and massively decreased my enjoyment of the game. But i guess thats just a skill issue.

UNDO THE RELOAD UPDATE 
please
I just want my go to game back.

negative.original:
Регистрация попаданий — дерьмо. Стреляешь в упор, прицел на враге — игре ♥♥♥♥♥, урон не проходит. Чувство, будто половина выстрелов просто исчезает.

Античит — дерьмо. Читеры бегают свободно, как у себя дома. Банят их редко, если вообще банят. Хочешь играть без этого цирка — иди на фейсит, регай акк, проходи верификацию с паспортными данными, покупай подписку, чтоб можно было получить все функции для +- комфортной игры. И даже там читеры есть. Просто меньше.

Матчмейкинг — дерьмо. Баланса нет: либо у тебя в команде нубы, которые не понимают, что происходит, либо против тебя задроты, которые разносят без шансов. Нормальных, ровных игр почти не бывает.

Итог: стрельба дерьмо, античит дерьмо, подбор игроков дерьмо. Играть в это = мазать лицо калом. Однако, оу щит, хи ви го эген

negative.original:
they ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ removed the ammo, oh my god

"early reload drops everything."

yea. sure. I wouldn't have believed this could even be an april fools update if a friend tried gaslight me into it. Just change a foundational mechanic that has been unchanged for 20 years that fundamentally breaks the way the game has been played for the past two decades by both professionals and casuals alike; why not?

If I want realism, I'll go to Insurgency. This is an arcade shooter and this update changes the way that I play perpetually and for the worst. Change it back.

update: I wrote this review after playing a game of it with the new ammo mechanics... I would like to apologize.

I was not harsh enough. This game is legitimately horrible now. I'm moving to Valorant until the change is reversed (it will be reversed because of how rancid playing like this is). I don't even like Valorant; the util in that game is class-locked and you can't change your class mid-match. However, at least it respects the players enough to have a working anticheat and not making groundbreaking changes to the game.

negative.original:
To the Valve Team:
In today’s Counter-Strike 2 update, the ammunition system underwent significant changes: leftover bullets are now discarded when reloading, reserve ammo is displayed as magazines, shells, or bullets depending on the weapon, the fill level of the current weapon is now shown below the ammo count, and reserve ammo counts for each weapon have been adjusted. These changes have seriously affected shooting feel and tactical flow in actual matches, disrupting players’ established habits. Many veteran players have reported that this system makes the game rely more on ammo management and memory rather than skill and strategy, reducing the sense of control over gameplay.
I understand the importance of innovation and optimization, but the core shooting experience is the soul of Counter-Strike 2. I sincerely urge Valve to carefully consider player feedback, revert or refine these changes, and restore the original weapon handling and tactical freedom, so that the game remains fair, exciting, and skill-based. The passion and trust of the player community are Counter-Strike 2’s most valuable assets—please do not compromise them lightly.
— Respectfully

Valve 团队：
今日的《Counter-Strike 2》更新中，弹药系统发生了重大改动：换弹时剩余子弹被丢弃、备弹显示方式改为弹匣/弹壳/子弹数量、当前武器填充量显示在弹药计数下方，同时各武器的备弹量也被调整。这些改动在实际对局中严重影响了射击手感与战术节奏，使玩家原有的操作习惯被打乱。许多资深玩家反映，这种机制让游戏更多依赖弹药管理和记忆，而非技术与策略，削弱了对技能的掌控感。
我理解创新和优化的重要性，但核心射击体验是《Counter-Strike 2》的灵魂。本人在此诚恳呼吁 Valve：请认真听取玩家反馈，撤回或优化此次改动，恢复原有的操作手感与战术自由度，让游戏继续公平、激情、靠技术说话。玩家的热情和信任，是《Counter-Strike 2》最宝贵的财富，请不要轻易破坏。
—— 此致

negative.original:
Its sad to see the state of this game,I was myself a CSGO player back in 2014 to 2016 and enjoyed playing even if I was a complete noob,but now the game is decaying by every day,more cheaters in,it got to a point where competitive uses a third party anti cheat and no on in ESports cares about CS2 rankings,and for this Valve is 100% guilty,we should not soften the guilt on them,they are a MULTIMILIONAIRE TEAM AND COMPANY...
Either way,nowadays Valve will only release skins get money from case opening and premier memberships,the people wwho payed almost 15 bucks should not be getting this decaying and rotten experience, right now in CS2 I would say I am getting matched up with cheaters almost every match,either in premier or normal competitive,this is unacceptable for a company as  big as Valve as I said earlier,CS2 is looking more as betting or investing platform than actual Counter Strike,the company got greedy,lost itss focus and doesnt care anymore about their players and fans,so yeah,I like the game but honestly,if u dont wanna get caught in a web of cheaters I dont recommend playing it becausse u will like it but it will be a torment of sadness because my hopes for Valve actaully giving a damn about the antti cheat and cheaters MASSIVE PROBLEM are down AF,so after all this.NO I DO NOT RECOMMEND BY ANY CHANCE PLAYING THIS GAME

negative.original:
Once a great game now unplayable.

The matchmaking experience is easily one of the worst aspects. Games often feel wildly unbalanced, with players of vastly different skill levels thrown into the same lobby. It’s not uncommon to see one team completely stomp the other with no real chance of a competitive match. This ruins the core appeal of Counter-Strike, which has always been about tight, skill-based competition. Queue times don’t justify the poor quality either—you wait just as long, only to end up in a match that feels decided before it even begins.

Then there’s the anti-cheat system, which frankly feels ineffective. Cheating has become far too noticeable, especially in higher ranks and Premier mode. Whether it’s blatant wallhacks or more subtle aim assistance, the lack of consistent enforcement makes it hard to take the competitive scene seriously. When players feel like matches are being decided by cheaters rather than skill, it completely kills motivation to play.

The Premier points system only adds to the frustration. The way points are gained or lost seems inconsistent and poorly explained. You can perform well individually, top frag, and still lose a significant number of points just because your team lost. 

Overall, Counter-Strike 2 currently struggles where it matters most: fair competition. Between broken matchmaking, weak anti-cheat, and a confusing ranking system, it’s hard to enjoy what should be a highly competitive and skill-driven game.

ngl this game is kinda turning into ♥♥♥♥. it doesn’t even feel like a proper skill game anymore, more like an addiction than anything else. you can play good, aim right, do everything you’re supposed to, and still get screwed by random stuff like hit reg, weird moments, or straight up cheaters.

some matches feel okay but then the next one is just full of sus players or just feels completely broken and you’re like wtf is even happening. it’s actually so frustrating when you’re trying to play seriously and the game just feels inconsistent.

and yeah people still play it but it lowkey feels like everyone’s just hooked, chasing that one good game over and over. not even fun half the time.

i mean the idea of cs is still good but rn it just feels broken, full of cheaters, and annoying to play.

Maybe it’s just my server, because the game has mostly positive reviews as of now 3/24/2026, but from my perspective, this is completely out of control. I was planning to buy Prime in the past, when I rarely encountered cheaters, but now I definitely won’t buy it.

And also, in casual mode, there’s an enormous number of bots that do nothing except spamming in the chat. this game is nearly unplayable.
